title: decision: an unfillable catch-up gap counts against follower_room.gone
description:
INVENTED, NOT FROM SPEC. Extends an existing field's meaning, so recorded
rather than resolved silently (AGENTS.md).

## The question

docs/design/mimi-catchup.md §5.1 has a hub answer 410 when the range a
follower asks for is older than it holds. The follower must surface that
-- silent loss is the thing the design exists to remove -- but mimid-server
had no way for the follower role to tell its own JMAP clients anything.

## The readings

1. A new counter in ProjectionCursor, e.g. `lost`, beside `gone`.
   Honest, but it is a fourth component in the cursor string
   ("{seq}.{member}.{gone}"), so every existing client's state fails to
   parse on upgrade and resyncs once for nothing.

2. Count it against follower_room.gone, the counter retention already
   bumps when it deletes an event. Chosen.

3. A notice or synthetic message in the room. Rejected: it would be
   content the hub never sent, in a room whose other content is
   authenticated, and the agent treats what a provider sends as
   untrusted precisely so a provider cannot inject into a room.

## Why 2

`gone`'s contract is already exactly what is needed: ProjectionCursor
documents that a state with another count cannot be followed by
/changes, because what it knew may be gone and seq may have gone back.
An unfillable gap is a hole in the middle of a room's history, which is
the thing /changes cannot express, and RFC 8620 §5.6
cannotCalculateChanges is its answer. To a client, "deleted by
retention" and "never received and never will be" are one fact: events
it will never see.

Only the count's CHANGING is read, never its magnitude (store/jmap.rs
compares `since.gone != current.gone` and `since.gone > current.gone`),
so it is a resync signal and not a number of anything. That is what
makes one-per-room sound even though nobody knows how many fanouts were
missed.

## Consequences

- ProjectionCursor::gone is redocumented to cover both, since its name
  and doc said "deleted" and now would have been a lie.
- Store::mark_gap_unfillable counts only on the FIRST mark, and returns
  whether it marked, so a retry does not move the cursor again. Counting
  per attempt would make every client resync forever. Tested
  (an_unfillable_gap_moves_what_clients_follow).
- Decisions mimid-1wgh.82 and mimid-1wgh.83 are about the retention
  case and are unaffected; this adds a second contributor to the same
  counter.
close_reason: Decided and implemented: an unfillable gap counts once against follower_room.gone, so a client's /changes refuses and it resyncs. Code points at this bead.
